When polymerizable compounds are mixed with toxic metals or metal compounds, several potential safety risks arise due to the reactivity of both components. Here's a breakdown of each option:

A. Explosion - Possible, as exothermic reactions can lead to pressure build-up.
B. Fire - Possible, especially if flammable substances are involved.
C. Flammable gas generation - Possible, if the reaction releases flammable gases.
D. Heat generation - Likely, as many chemical reactions are exothermic.
E. Innocuous and non-flammable gas generation - Unlikely, as the presence of toxic metals suggests hazardous reactions.
F. May be hazardous but unknown - Possible, as specific reactions depend on the compounds involved.
G. Solubilization of toxic substance - Possible, if the reaction dissolves toxic metals.
H. Toxic gas generation - Possible, if gases released are harmful.
I. Violent polymerization - Possible, as metal catalysts can accelerate polymerization.

Given the typical risks involved, the most likely correct answers are: [ANSWER]A,B,C,D,G,H,I[/ANSWER].
